title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy (How Well the Study Treatment Works) of ABBV-2294 in Adult Participants With Systemic Sclerosis That Are Currently Receiving Local Standard of Care Treatment, and to Determine the Best Dose of ABBV-2294 to be Evaluated Further.
off: A Phase 2b/3 Multicenter, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of ABBV-2294 (Combination of ABBV-722 and Upadacitinib) in Adult Patients With Systemic Sclerosis
summary:
Systemic sclerosis (SSc), also called scleroderma, is a rare long-term autoimmune disease that causes the body to make too much collagen (scar tissue), leading to hard, thick skin and sometimes damage to organs such as the lungs, heart, kidneys, or digestive system. An autoimmune disease is a condition where the body's immune system, which normally protects against germs, mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissues and organs.

The study has 2 parts. The main goal of Part 1 is to evaluate the safety and efficacy (how well the study treatment works) of ABBV-2294 (combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib) in adult participants with SSc that are currently receiving local standard of care treatment, and to determine the best dose of ABBV-2294 to be evaluated further. The main goal of Part 2 is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the dose of ABBV-2294 determined in Part 1 when compared to placebo (looks like the study treatment but has no medicine in it) in adult patients with SSc that are currently receiving local standard of care treatment. Participants will undergo trial-related procedures throughout the study which may include physical exams, questionnaires, scans and imaging, and blood and urine tests.

ABBV-2294 (combination of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib) is an investigational drug being developed for the treatment of SSc in adult participants. At the start of Part 1, participants will be randomly assigned to receive Dose 1 of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib given together, Dose 2 of ABBV-722 and upadacitinib given together, ABBV-722 given alone, upadacitinib given alone, or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants that complete 52 weeks of treatment will be invited to join a 56-week extension period.

Participants that join Part 2 will be randomly assigned to receive either ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1) or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants that complete 52 weeks of treatment will be invited to join a 104-week extension period. All participants that join the extension will receive ABBV-2294.

Participants 18 years of age and older diagnosed with Systemic sclerosis (SSc). Around 580 participants will be enrolled at approximately 200 sites worldwide.

Participants will receive upadacitinib and/or ABBV-722 oral tablets (or matching placebo) for 52 weeks in Part 1 with an optional 56-week extension period. Part 2 participants will receive ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1) or matching placebo for 52 weeks with an optional 104-week extension period of open label ABBV-2294 (dose determined in Part 1).

There may be higher treatment burden for participants in this trial compared to their standard of care due to study procedures. Participants will attend regular visits during the study at a hospital or clinic, including screening, baseline, and scheduled visits. The effects of the treatment will be checked by medical assessments, blood tests, checking for side effects, and completing questionnaires.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants must voluntarily sign and date an informed consent, approved by an IEC/IRB, prior to the initiation of any Screening or study-specific procedures.
* Adults \>= 18 years of age at the time of the Screening Visit (subjects must also meet the legal age of majority per local law).
* Participants are willing and able to comply with procedures required in the protocol.
* Participants must not be incarcerated and must be freely willing and able to provide informed consent. Examples of subjects unable to freely provide informed consent may include some adults under legal protection measure (e.g., under guardianship/curatorship) or unable to express their consent and select adults under psychiatric care. Investigator's discretion should be applied.
* Participants must fulfil the ACR/EULAR 2013 classification criteria for SSc

Exclusion Criteria:

* Other autoimmune connective tissue diseases, overlap syndromes, or SSc mimics (e.g., scleromyxedema, eosinophilic fasciitis), except scleroderma-associated myopathy and associated Sjögren disease.
* Pulmonary disease with predicted FVC \< 45% at Screening.
* Predicted diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO, Hb corrected) \< 25% at Screening.
* History of scleroderma renal crisis within the last 6 months.
* History of severe gastric antral telangiectasias (watermelon stomach).

x.titre: ABBV-2294 (ABBV-722 et upadacitinib) dans la sclérodermie systémique
x.question: L'association ABBV-2294 améliore-t-elle la réponse composite rCRISS-25 à 52 semaines chez des adultes atteints de sclérodermie systémique, et quelle est la dose à retenir ?
x.contexte:
La sclérodermie systémique (ScS) est une maladie auto-immune rare caractérisée par une production excessive de collagène. Elle entraîne une induration cutanée et une atteinte d'organes (poumon, cœur, rein, tube digestif). Les traitements disponibles ciblent surtout certaines manifestations, comme l'atteinte pulmonaire interstitielle, et aucun ne modifie à lui seul l'ensemble de l'évolution de la maladie.

L'ABBV-2294 associe l'ABBV-722 et l'upadacitinib, un inhibiteur de JAK déjà utilisé dans d'autres maladies inflammatoires. Le registre ne détaille pas la cible de l'ABBV-722. Le rationnel est d'agir sur plusieurs voies inflammatoires et fibrosantes à la fois.

Cet essai de phase 2/3 d'AbbVie, randomisé et en triple insu, comporte deux parties. La partie 1 compare deux doses d'ABBV-2294, l'ABBV-722 seul, l'upadacitinib seul et un placebo, pour évaluer la sécurité et l'efficacité et choisir la dose. La partie 2 compare la dose retenue au placebo. Il inclut environ 580 adultes sous traitement standard local, remplissant les critères ACR/EULAR 2013.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait montrer si une association ciblée améliore l'évolution globale de la ScS, mesurée par un indice composite. Elle permettrait aussi d'isoler la contribution de chaque composant par rapport à l'association.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de sclérodermie systémique (critères ACR/EULAR 2013) sous traitement standard local.

Consentement éclairé signé, capacité à le donner librement
Volonté et capacité de respecter les procédures du protocole
exclusion: Autre connectivite, syndrome de chevauchement ou imitation de ScS (scléromyxœdème, fasciite à éosinophiles), sauf myopathie sclérodermique et syndrome de Sjögren associé
Crise rénale sclérodermique dans les 6 derniers mois
Antécédent d'estomac pastèque (ectasies vasculaires antrales sévères)
